title: streaming_collect is re-imported locally inside iter_chunked_frames though it is already imported at module level
description: iter_chunked_frames performs a function-local `from haute._polars_utils import (bounded_collect_batches, streaming_collect, temporary_streaming_chunk_size)`. However `streaming_collect` is already imported at module scope on line 27 (`from haute._polars_utils import DEFAULT_STREAMING_CHUNK_SIZE, streaming_collect`) and is used elsewhere in the module at lines 670 and 1029 via that module-level binding. The local re-import of `streaming_collect` shadows the identical module-level name with no behavioral difference. Only `bounded_collect_batches` and `temporary_streaming_chunk_size` genuinely need the local import (they are not imported at module level). This is incidental redundancy, not a correctness issue.
evidence: Line 27: `from haute._polars_utils import DEFAULT_STREAMING_CHUNK_SIZE, streaming_collect`. Line 864 re-imports the same `streaming_collect` inside iter_chunked_frames. grep of `streaming_collect` in chunking.py shows usages at 670 and 1029 (both resolvable from the module-level import) plus the redundant local import at 864.
est_reduction: -1 name from the local import tuple (drop `streaming_collect` from line 864, keeping bounded_collect_batches and temporary_streaming_chunk_size which are not module-level).
behavior_preservation: Identical: the module-level streaming_collect (line 27) is the same object; removing the shadowing local re-import leaves all call sites bound to the same function. No call site references differ.
